easy.def: To go in front to show the way.
examples: I lead the way to the door.
The guide led us through the cave.
A duck leads her ducklings.

more.def: To go first and show others where to go.
examples: The scout leader led the hikers up the trail.
A mother duck leads her ducklings across the road.
The guide led us through the old castle.

easy.def: To be in charge of a group.
examples: Who will lead the team?
She leads our club.
He led the class in song.

more.def: To be in charge of a group of people.
examples: Maya will lead the school band this year.
The queen led her people with kindness.
Who wants to lead the meeting?

easy.def: A soft, heavy, gray metal.
examples: Old pipes were made of lead.
Lead is very heavy.
Fishing weights are made of lead.

more.def: A soft, heavy, bluish-gray metal used to make weights and some batteries.
examples: Fishers use small weights made of lead.
Lead is very heavy for its size.
Long ago, many water pipes were made of lead.

easy.def: The person in front who shows the way.
examples: Today I am the line leader.
The leader of the band waved a stick.
Follow the leader!

more.def: A person who guides or is in charge of a group.
examples: A good leader listens to everyone on the team.
The team chose her as leader because she is fair.
The scout leader showed us how to build a fire.

easy.def: To find out how to do something.
examples: I learn new words at school.
She learned to ride a bike.
We are learning to swim.

more.def: To get new knowledge or a new skill by studying, practicing or being taught.
examples: Children learn to read by sounding out letters and words.
He learned how to play the piano by practicing every day.
Scientists are always learning new things about space.

easy.def: To go away from a place.
examples: We leave at noon.
She left the room.
The bus leaves soon.

more.def: To go away from a place or a person.
examples: The train leaves the station at nine o'clock.
Please leave the room quietly when the bell rings.
We left the beach before the tide came in.

easy.def: To let something stay where it is.
examples: Leave your shoes here.
I left my hat at home.
Do not leave the door open.

more.def: To let something stay in a place, or to forget to take it with you.
examples: Leave your boots by the door so you do not track in mud.
I left my lunch box on the school bus.
Please leave some cake for your brother.

easy.def: On the side of the body opposite the right.
examples: Raise your left hand.
Turn left here.
My left shoe is wet.

more.def: On the side of your body that is opposite the right side.
examples: Most people hold a fork in their left hand.
The bakery is on the left side of the street.
She tied her left shoe, then her right one.

easy.def: The part of your body you walk on.
examples: My leg hurts.
A dog has four legs.
She crossed her legs.

more.def: One of the long body parts that people and animals use to stand and walk.
examples: A spider has eight legs.
The horse stood on its strong legs.
She stretched her legs after the long drive.

easy.def: A part that holds something up.
examples: The table has four legs.
One chair leg is loose.
The leg of the bed is wobbly.

more.def: A long, thin part that holds up a piece of furniture.
examples: The table leg is wobbly.
The chair has four wooden legs.
The stool's third leg was shorter than the other two.

easy.def: Allowed by the law.
examples: It is legal to drive at sixteen.
That is legal.
A legal sign.

more.def: Allowed by the law, or having to do with the law.
examples: It is legal to ride a bike on this road.
The park has legal parking spaces.
It is not legal to cross the street here.

easy.def: A very old story that people still tell.
examples: There is a legend about a dragon in this cave.
The legend is about a brave girl.
Grandpa told us a legend.

more.def: An old story passed down over many years that may or may not be true.
examples: According to legend, a giant made these hills.
The legend says a monster lives in the lake.
Many legends are told about the brave king.

easy.def: Time when you learn something.
examples: We have a swimming lesson.
The lesson was fun.
The music lesson is at four.

more.def: A period of time when a teacher teaches something.
examples: I have a piano lesson on Tuesday.
The math lesson was about fractions.
She takes swimming lessons at the pool.

easy.def: Something you learn from an event.
examples: I learned a lesson.
The story has a lesson.
Never again, he learned his lesson.

more.def: Something that you learn from something that happened.
examples: He learned a lesson about being careful.
The lesson of the story is to share.
Missing the bus taught her a lesson.

easy.def: To say yes to something.
examples: Mom let me stay up.
Please let me help.
Let the dog out.

more.def: To give someone permission, or to allow something to happen.
examples: My dad let me pick the movie on Friday night.
She opened the window to let fresh air into the room.
Do not let the cat get out of the house.

easy.def: A note you write and mail to someone.
examples: I wrote a letter to Grandma.
The mail carrier brought a letter.
She mailed the letter.

more.def: A written message that is put in an envelope and sent to someone.
examples: She wrote a letter to her pen pal in Spain.
The mail carrier dropped a letter in our box.
He opened the letter and read it twice.

easy.def: A sign used in writing words.
examples: A is a letter.
Say the letter B.
Which letter comes next?

more.def: One of the symbols, such as A or B, that are used to write words.
examples: There are twenty-six letters in the alphabet.
Her name starts with the letter M.
He learned to write each letter.

easy.def: How high something is.
examples: The water level is high.
The river level rose.
Her reading level is high.

more.def: The height of something, or how much of something there is.
examples: The water level in the lake went down.
The noise level in the cafeteria is high.
Her reading level is very advanced.

easy.def: One part in a series of steps.
examples: I beat the third level of the game.
The parking lot has three levels.
She reached the next level.

more.def: One floor of a building or one stage in a game or a series.
examples: The parking garage has four levels.
I finally passed level five of the game.
Each level is harder than the last.

easy.def: Flat, with no bumps.
examples: The floor is level.
Put the board on a level surface.
A level field is good for soccer.

more.def: Flat and even, with no part higher than another.
examples: We set up the tent on level ground.
The shelf was not level, so the marbles rolled off.
The pool table must be level.
